title: Redwood Discovery - Meridian Health latency & throughput
customer_attendees: Dr. Priya Rao - Head of ML
summary: Initial latency and throughput discovery for Meridian Health evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Focus on p95 SLOs, concurrency targets, streaming behaviour, token/sec benchmarks. Customer concerned about PHI, VPC/private deployment, SOC2 and KMS. Agreed next step: Redwood to run a benchmark with customer prompts, share security pack and pricing, schedule technical deep dive within 1 week.
topics: security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, data residency
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-11-18 15:32 UTC | Duration: 47m | Attendees: Sanjay (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Priya (Meridian Head ML), Ethan (Platform), Marta (Security), Alex (Product)

Summary (auto): talk about p95, concurrency, run a benchmark, share security docs - action items at end.

00:00 Sanjay: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll do a 1 min intro, Redwood is the inference platform, we do hosted, dedicated and private deployments, and lena will go into latency/throughput details.
00:22 Priya: great thanks, we mostly want to understand if hosted can meet our p95 targets for inference on clinical summarization flows, otherwise we'll need dedicated or private.
00:30 Lena: cool, can you share the target numbers that matter for you? p95 numbers, concurrency, token lengths, streaming?
00:38 Priya: yeah our main SLO is p95 end-to-end generation under 300ms for short-turn queries (~32 tokens). For longer streaming summaries (~600-1k tokens) we need stable tail latency, p95 under 1.5s for the initial chunk and roughly 500-800 tokens/sec sustained per model instance.
00:57 Ethan: also we expect concurrency of 80-120 active concurrent users in peak, with bursts to 250. Important: each user does a small request then sometimes a long streaming summarization job, and we want predictable latency for the short ones.
01:12 Lena: okay that's helpful. For hosted, we publish profiles for verified models showing p95 numbers at given sequence lengths and concurrency. For example, a 32-token completion on our curated 7B quantized model is ~120-180ms p95 on our hosted pools at 1-5 concurrency, but at 100 concurrency you'll see batching behaviors.
01:30 Priya: batching sounds like it could add variance. we need the short path to remain low latency. can you guarantee no batching for low-latency tiers?
01:38 Sanjay: we have latency-tier routing policies — you can route to a latency-first pool (smaller batch windows, reserved capacity). That's what our Dedicated offering does by default. Hosted also exposes a latency path for customers with small footprints, but at very large concurrency dedicated is more predictable.
01:56 Lena: exactly. for hosted we do continuous batching with configurable max latency windows; typical window is 10-30ms, but at high concurrency effective batch sizes increase which can add to tail latency. Dedicated lets you pin GPU pools and set autoscale/burst rules so p95 remains stable.
02:12 Marta: quick security note — Meridian handles PHI, so we need private deployment or at minimum VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for keys. Hosted with BYOK is okay only if audit logs and data residency controls are in place. do you have SOC2 and ISO attestation?
02:26 Sanjay: yes SOC2 type II. we provide audit logs, and our private option supports customer-managed KMS and on-prem packaging. we'll share the security pack after the call.
02:36 Alex: can you summarize the throughput numbers — tokens per second we should expect for a given cluster size?
02:42 Lena: rough numbers: on an A100-equivalent instance serving a 7B quantized model, you can expect ~2k-5k tokens/sec single-instance peak for streaming workloads depending on batch and token size. For 13B models quantized, closer to 1k-2k tokens/sec. These are very workload-dependent though — prompt lengths, temperature, and repetition matter.
03:05 Ethan: do you have a spreadsheet or benchmark harness we can run against? we have 50 representative prompts and expected output lengths, we can share.
03:12 Sanjay: yes, we typically run a token/sec and p95 benchmark using your prompt set, measure cold/warm cache, KV prefix caching, also measure streaming latency (time-to-first-token, time-per-token). we'll run a hosted pilot and a dedicated proof-of-concept so you can compare.
03:28 Priya: timeline — we want a decision in 4 weeks. we need results from a realistic bench in 10 days ideally.
03:35 Lena: that's achievable. we'll schedule the benchmark run this week, need a dataset and API access (we can provide a temporary test key).
03:42 Marta: for security, before any test keys we need an NDA and for dedicated/private any network setup docs.
03:48 Sanjay: understood. we'll send NDA + security pack + initial pricing.
03:54 (short crosstalk)
04:10 Lena: digging into the p95 tradeoffs — if your short request is 32 tokens, we can tune batching to favor latency: small max batch size, 0ms batching window, dedicate warm instances (no cold-start). That gives p95 similar to single requests, but cost increases. If you accept slightly higher p95 we can batch aggressively for cost-savings.
04:35 Priya: what's cold-start impact? we do lots of spiky traffic overnight, cannot have 800ms cold-starts on short queries.
04:40 Lena: cold-starts can be mitigated with warm pools and autoscaling policies (pre-warm). Dedicated has stronger guarantees; hosted can pre-warm on request but it's less predictable across regions at scale.
04:54 Ethan: what about streaming semantics — time-to-first-token matters. can you keep TTF less than 150ms for summaries?
05:00 Lena: yes our runtime supports low TTF with KV cache and early token generation pipelines. For longer outputs we stream chunked tokens; p95 TTF of 120-200ms is realistic on tuned setups. we'll capture that in the benchmark.
05:18 Alex: do you support function/tool calling and structured output? we rely on deterministic tool sequences and partial outputs.
05:24 Lena: yes we support structured outputs and function calling; streaming includes partial JSON chunks but you need to handle backfill when tokens arrive out-of-order — we'll provide SDK helpers.
05:36 Priya: back to numbers: to hit 300ms p95 for 32 tokens at 120 concurrency, what does your cluster look like?
05:45 Lena: depends on model. ballpark: for a 7B quantized model, you'd need a few dedicated GPUs (4-8) with reserved capacity and small batch windows. For 120 concurrent short requests the effective token/sec requirement is modest but the main driver is concurrency handling and prewarmed instances. we'll run load simulation to give a specific sizing.
06:05 Ethan: we also want to monitor per-token cost — e.g., tokens/sec vs $/token. can you provide cost profiles for hosted and dedicated?
06:12 Sanjay: yes we'll share cost estimates. dedicated is cheaper at steady high-throughput, hosted is lower friction for small pilots. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization to cut costs 30-60% per token.
06:28 Marta: encryption at rest and in-transit — do you support customer-managed KMS?
06:33 Sanjay: yes for Private and Dedicated; hosted has BYOK where KMS holds keys but we recommend private if regulatory controls require full isolation.
06:42 Priya: any competitor mentions? we've been talking to MajorCloudAI and Infrastack — they promise low latency but limited observability and less mature rollout controls.
06:52 Lena: on observability — our console exposes token-level breakdowns, per-route p95, and tracing hooks. we'll include a sample dashboard in the security/ops pack.
07:05 Alex: what about concurrency bursts up to 250 — how does autoscaling behave? can bursts be absorbed without impacting p95 for short calls?
07:14 Lena: with burst policies you can reserve headroom and use burst capacity; Dedicated supports fast scale-up and predictable headroom. For hosted, transient bursts may increase p95 briefly unless you buy burst capacity. We'll show autop-scaling timelines in the benchmark report.
07:30 Priya: ok next steps explicitly?
07:34 Sanjay: we'll run a benchmark (hosted + dedicated) on your 50 prompts, measure cold/warm/stream, token/sec, p95 for short and long flows. deliverables: spreadsheet with raw metrics, sizing recommendation, pricing for Dedicated reserve and Private option, security pack (SOC2, ISO, KMS, SSO/SAML), and proposed SOW.
07:52 Marta: please include network diagrams for VPC peering and details on audit logs retention.
07:58 Sanjay: will do.
08:02 (end)

Action items noted in summary: send NDA, security docs, run benchmarks, schedule deep dive.
